brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit (a surface/unit for shelving books)
requirements.evidence: 3-wide 2-storey unit: bases piece:-1,0,0;half-n, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;half-n below level-1 bases and top covers cover:-1,0,1;half-n;top, cover:0,0,1;full;top, cover:1,0,1;half-n;top forming the shelf deck, staged with prop:1 (book-row) and prop:2 (book). Shape is a shelf, but see load-rating requirement.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Configurator checks fit/collisions only and knows nothing about materials, strength or load ratings; parts are 3D-printed plastic in a user-chosen material. No 50 kg rating can be certified or claimed from this build, so it should not be relied on for 50 kg.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut on piece:-1,0,0;half-n and drawer:0#1,0#cut on piece:1,0,0;half-n

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell-wide, 2-storey shelf unit: two classic drawers (drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut) in half-n bases at the bottom, a full-width covered deck (covers at level 1) on top, capped (capOpenFaces) and joint-locked, staged with a row of books and a lying book. The check_build mesh gate is clear. The 50 kg rating cannot be met: the parts are 3D-printed plastic in a user-chosen material and the configurator checks fit/collisions only, with no strength, load-rating or material data, so no load capacity is claimed — the shape is a shelf (books staged on the deck), but it must not be relied on to hold 50 kg.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building a book shelf with two drawers — I’ll check what’s on the bench and what drawer/shelf pieces fit, noting I can’t certify a 50 kg load for printed parts.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

warnings.message: 1 part(s) could slide apart (1 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.

offersNear.note: Open offers at the base just added (valid until the next change): apply one by its socket, no find_sockets needed.

outcomes.message: a base carries its OWN kind: the cell below is North half, so only that goes on top. The batch was rolled back: details.steps is the batch again with this op changed.
accepted, then undone with the rest of the batch: not on the build

result.rollback: Nothing in this batch is on the build: one op was refused, so every op in it was undone. Fix or drop the refused op and send the batch again (a refusal with details.steps gives the whole batch with it fixed: send those ops as one apply); refs and offers from this batch do not exist.

events.text: Three-cell shelf deck is on, with two drawers underneath. Now I’ll cap and lock it and stage books on the deck — the 50 kg rating stays unproven for printed plastic.
